Although their favored *M/L*$_{\rm F814W}$ values decrease with increasing BH mass, both models systematically overpredict the rotation of the $^{12}$CO(2$-$1) CND—either within the inner $0.6\ensuremath{''}$ for $M_{\rm BH} = 2.0\times10^{9}$ M$_{\odot}$ or across the entire disk for $M_{\rm BH} \approx 1.2\times10^{10}$ M$_{\odot}$.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Thick disk geometry, radially varying turbulent velocity dispersion sigma_gas(r), radially varying M/L_F814W(r), unmasked dust in F814W, and F555W stellar mass MGE: tested as alternatives to evaluate systematic uncertainties.

evidence.quote: Several additional sources of uncertainty are inherent to dynamical modeling, including (i) the adopted distance to NGC 4061, (ii) the assumption of a thick disk (implemented via the $z$-coordinate perpendicular to the disk plane), (iii) the turbulent velocity dispersion of the gas, (iv) the disk inclination, (v) possible radial variations in the mass-to-light ratio, (vi) the construction of the stellar mass model without dust masking, and (vii) the use of an alternative photometric band.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Achieved resolving power zeta = 2 r_soi / theta_FWHM ~ 2 (matching the criterion zeta >= 2 for precise M_BH measurements), verified Gaussian-like MCMC posterior convergence over 10^5 iterations, confirmed low velocity residuals (<= 15 km s^-1), and ran extensive systematic tests across 7 potential error sources.

evidence.quote: All distributions exhibit Gaussian-like shapes, demonstrating that the MCMC optimization of our KINMS models achieved robust convergence.
Observations with $\zeta \geq 2$ (i.e., $\theta_{\rm FWHM} \leq r_{\rm soi}$) are generally sufficient to yield precise $M_{\rm BH}$ determinations (cite: North19; Boizelle21).
In the case of NGC 4061, our ALMA data correspond to $\zeta \approx 2$, indicating that the dynamical-$M_{\rm BH}$ measurement presented in this work is robust.

limitations_admitted.value: The wide range of published distances to NGC 4061 (68–112 Mpc in NED) introduces a ~37% systematic uncertainty in M_BH, dominating the total error budget.

evidence.quote: Since the inferred $M_{\rm BH}$ scales linearly with the assumed distance ($M_{\rm BH} \propto D$), the wide range of distance estimates for NGC 4061 (68–112 Mpc; NED)—primarily based on optical and near-infrared light curves of the Type Ia supernova SN 2008bf—constitutes the dominant source of uncertainty in our $M_{\rm BH}$ measurement.
The spread in published distances introduces a systematic uncertainty of $\approx$37% in $M_{\rm BH}$.

evidence.quote: Overall, adopting the F555W-based stellar mass model introduces an additional uncertainty of approximately 20% in the inferred SMBH mass for NGC 4061, likely reflecting the greater sensitivity of the F555W band to dust attenuation compared to the F814W band.

limitations_admitted.value: Direct event-horizon-scale imaging of the NGC 4061 SMBH (~0.4 uas) is impossible even with ngEHT (~10 uas resolution).

evidence.quote: We also should note that a $\sim$$10^{9}$ M$_{\odot}$ SMBH at $\sim$107 Mpc has an event-horizon angular size of only $\sim$0.4 $\mu$as, far below the $\sim$10 $\mu$as reach of ngEHT (cite: Johnson2023; Shlentsova2024), making direct horizon-scale imaging impossible at that distance.

referee_caveats_inferred: Inconsistency in the reported 1.3 mm continuum RMS noise: Section 2.2 text states sigma_cont = 120 uJy beam^-1, whereas Table 1 lists Sensitivity = 0.02 mJy per beam (20 uJy beam^-1).
Section 2.3 states 'The final self-calibrated, cleaned cube shares the same synthesized beam as the 1.3 mm continuum image', but no self-calibration procedure is mentioned in Section 2.1 or 2.2.

In Section 4.5.6 (dust-unmasked F814W MGE test), the derived M_BH drops to (7.41 +/- 1.92) x 10^8 M_odot and (6.92 +/- 1.16) x 10^8 M_odot (~37-41% lower than the fiducial 1.17 x 10^9 M_odot) while M/L_F814W jumps from 3.46 to ~5.5, yet the text characterizes this as 'close agreement' and 'negligible impact'.

In Section 2.4, the text states that velocity dispersion outside the central boxy region is 0 <= sigma_LOS <= 70 km s^-1 and that 'Section 4.4 best-fitting dynamical models yield an intrinsic velocity dispersion of 18-22 km s^-1', whereas Table 4 and Section 4.5.3 report best-fit sigma_gas = 13.91 km s^-1 (SkySampler) and 15.51 km s^-1 (Gaussian).

In Section 4.7, the M_BH-sigma_e regression uses 35 galaxies, but Table 7 lists Fairall 49 with no sigma_e value ('-') and NGC 4061 with no sigma_e uncertainty ('290 +/- ...'); how missing values or uncertainties were handled in scipy.stats.linregress (which is an unweighted ordinary least squares routine) is not explained.
